description:
FILED s446k (Opus, agent K of round 5).  The #463 items 3-5 repair
(`Pl::Parser2::_repair_punct_glob_name`) covers a glob named by a digit run or
by a single punctuation character.  Two measured spellings are NOT covered,
both by design:

1. `*^R = *caretRglobwithnoscalar;`  (t/re/pat.t:1715, 1 census drop)
   PPI: Operator(*) Operator(^) Word(R).  The name is NOT `^` -- `^R` is
   perl's caret convention for chr(18), the same one `$^R` uses, so this needs
   the #412 caret-name machinery (`_block_caret_name`), not the punctuation
   set.  A naive `*{'^'}R` rewrite would be a SILENT WRONG.
   NB: PCL's `$^R` itself is already broken -- `$^R = 7; print $^R` prints
   nothing (probed s446k) -- so fixing the glob without the variable buys
   nothing.  Size both together.

2. `tie my $var4 => 'main', *];`    (t/op/tie_fetch_count.t:189)
   PPI makes the `]` a Structure token, not an Operator, so the two-token
   merge does not see it; a Structure-aware arm would have to be sure it is
   not closing a real subscript.

BAR: the s371 rule -- these shapes occur once each in the whole population, so
guard rows in `Pl/t/punct-glob-name-01.t` plus an inverse run ARE the bar, and
each needs its own perl probe (what does `*^R = *g` actually alias?).


DONE s448o (Opus, agent O of round 6), commit 9142bdb (rebased).  BOTH items.

ITEM 1 (`*^R`).  Probed first, as the task asks -- and the probe is the whole
design:
  *  `our $s="V"; *^R = *s; print $^R`  prints V, and a later `$^R = "w"`
     writes through to `$s`: perl aliases the WHOLE glob.
  *  `${"\cR"}` IS `$^R`; `${"^R"}` is a DIFFERENT variable (stash keys 0x12
     vs "^R").
  *  `"" . *^R` is `*main::` followed by chr(18) -- eight characters.  So the
     typeglob's NAME is the control character, and must stay that.
So the repair emits the CONTROL CHARACTER (`*{'<chr18>'}`), the symbolic
spelling the compiler already lowers, and the two spellings meet in the
RUNTIME: a new `%p-slot-name` maps a one-control-character glob name onto PCL's
`$^R` spelling at the ONE step that turns a glob NAME into a slot SYMBOL name
(four glob functions plus %p-symref-symbol, all through the one helper) --
never at the typeglob name itself.  Interning "$^R" in MAIN finds the exported
pcl::|$^R|, so a caret glob assigned inside `package Foo` reaches main's cell as
perl forces it to (probed).  BONUS, a divergence nobody had filed: `${"\cR"}`
and `$^R` were two different cells in PCL and are now one, as in perl.

Only a Word of ONE upper-case letter is taken.  PPI hands the whole following
word over as one token, so `*^Rfoo` arrives as Word("Rfoo") -- which is `*^R`
followed by `foo`, not a glob name -- and a longer Word keeps dropping loudly.

ITEM 2 (`*]`).  A safe discriminator DOES exist and PPI supplies it: a bracket
that closes a real subscript, list or constructor is the `finish` of a
PPI::Structure, while an orphan is parked in a PPI::Statement::UnmatchedBrace.
Measured over subscripts, slices, anon constructors, list slices and ($x)[0],
it separates them exactly, and a `(*)` PROTOTYPE never reaches the arm at all
(PPI lexes it as one Token::Prototype).  Only CLOSERS ] ) } are in the set:
`*{` is the deref-block spelling and must never be claimed, an opener is never
orphaned so the test could not protect it, and deleting a `;` would take the
statement terminator with it.

MEASUREMENTS.  Census: t/re/pat.t 3 -> 2 drops (arms disabled 3, enabled 2),
edited row by row; totals 34/89 -> 34/88, and the header's stale pre-s446k
"73 files, 167 drops" recomputed from the rows while there.  The `*]` half
changes NO census row and never could: t/op/tie_fetch_count.t is refused whole
at line 169 (`~~`), emits nothing, and has never had one -- so the s371 rule
applies and its guard rows plus the probe ARE its bar.  Emission A/B vs main
over perl's t/ + cpan-tests (988 files): pat.t the only DIFF attributable here,
one hunk, RCDIFF 0.  corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111.  Guard
Pl/t/punct-glob-name-01.t 8 -> 12 rows, inverse-run TWICE (parser arms off: the
three positives fail, the negative passes; runtime map off: the two caret rows
fail).  ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§26 extended; docs/ppi-bug-report.t 36 -> 38.

RESIDUE, FILED AS #602 and NOT caret-shaped: `*A = *B` does not CLEAR the slots
B lacks -- perl replaces the glob, PCL copies bound slots only.  That is why the
fourth line of the *^R probe still differs (`*^R = *globwithnoscalar` leaves
$^R alone where perl makes it undef), and it is the same shortcoming
not-supported.md names for English's @ARG.  t/re/pat.t:1717's own assertion
(`is $^R, 42`) still cannot pass either way: it needs (?{...}) regex code
blocks, which are blessed not-supported.
subject: #463 residue: `*^R` (a CARET-named glob) and `*]` still drop -- the two glob-name spellings the s446k punctuation repair deliberately leaves alone
